newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iran minister holds talks in Turkey on tense ties.
newsitem.headline: Iran minister holds talks in Turkey on tense ties.

text.p: Iran's deputy foreign minister Alaeddin Boroujerdi met Turkish President Suleyman Demirel amid growing tension between the two neighbours in the wake of Turkey's month-long incursion into northern Iraq.
A spokesman for the president said the two had met but gave no details of the contents of their meeting.
Earlier Boroujerdi met foreign ministry officials and Fehim Adak, a state minister and close aide to Necmettin Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister.

The Turkish military has accused Iran, among other countries, of supplying separatist rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) with sophisticated anti-aircraft missiles used to shoot down two Turkish army helicopters.
Iran has publically denied the accusations.

"We want to help with the security concerns of a friendly and neighbouring country like Turkey and we are ready to make every effort in this area," state-run Anatolian news agency quoted Boroujerdi as saying.

Turkish media reported that Iran has demanded Turkey's forces not enter the Hakurk region of northern Iraq, near the point where the three neighbouring countries meet. The troops, backed by air power, entered Iraq on May 14.
Erbakan, locked in a feud with the military over Islamic activism and his desire for closer ties with Iran, also warned the army about the region, the media said.
"We have got very close to the Iranian border. It is a very sensitive area. We must be very careful," the daily Sabah quoted Erbakan as telling the army's chief of staff on Monday.

The Iraqi National Congress, citing satellite telephone links with the area, said about 2,000 guerrillas of the PKK, backed by other local forces, had clashed with the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), allied with Ankara, close to the Iranian border.
The PKK were joined by the Kurdish Hizbollah, the Kurdistan Conservative Party and the Kurdistan Social Democratic Party -- all believed to have close ties to Iran, the INC spokesman said.
Between 700 to 1,000 PKK guerrillas had earlier crossed into Hakurk from neighbouring Iran armed with Soviet-designed Grad multiple missile launchers, he said.
The region, however, remains closed to all journalists, making any independent confirmation impossible.
